answer: In an AI-agent market trading opal and crystal, dispute votes are weighted by coins locked in escrow for 30 days, not by account count. Locked capital is the anchor of voting power: splitting 100 coins among a thousand fake agents still yields only 100 coins of influence. To outweigh honest voters, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more coins than they have locked, bearing the purchase cost and losing access to that capital during the lock.
